items.title: Iraqi forces enter Jurf al Sakhar militia stronghold as PM seeks to consolidate power
items.summary: Iraqi security forces entered Jurf al Sakhar, a longstanding stronghold of the Iran-backed Kataib Hezbollah militia, on November 20 following an investigation into oil smuggling. The continued presence of militia fighters and the deployment of Popular Mobilization Forces brigades raise questions about whether Baghdad can establish full government control over the area. The post Iraqi forces enter Jurf al Sakhar militia stronghold as PM seeks to consolidate power appeared first on FDD's Long War Journal.

items.summary: Israeli air strikes on the devastated Gaza Strip killed Brigadier General Naeem Abu Nahel, director-general of the Palestinian territory's Internal Security Service on Tuesday, the ministry said. Another six people, including two police officers and a 17-year-old teenager, were killed in Israeli strikes across the enclave.

items.title: Spain set to head to polls in snap election that could boost far right
items.summary: Socialist Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez seeks to thwart grim polls as polarised Spain holds an election on Sunday that could propel the opposition conservative Popular Party (PP) and the far right to power. The outcome will be closely watched across Europe as it opens a cycle of elections over the next 12 months that could reshape the balance of power within the European Union.

items.title: Colombia: Guterres urges renewed commitment to landmark peace deal
items.summary: UN Secretary-General António Guterres has commended Colombia for progress achieved in the decade since a landmark accord known as the Final Peace Agreement ended more than 50 years of insurgency but stressed the need to fully implement its provisions.

items.summary: UN Secretary-General António Guterres on Monday called on Member States to begin discussions on a multilateral framework for managing the risks of artificial intelligence (AI), warning that the technology is driving “the biggest transfer of power in the history of humankind”.

items.title: COP31 ends without climate pact as UN chief warns there is ‘no ambiguity in the science’

items.title: Senegal regain AFCON title after successful appeal at sport arbitration court
items.summary: The Court of Arbitration for Sport on Tuesday ruled in favour of Senegal in the appeal to reclaim the Africa Cup of Nations title, 10 months after a chaotic final against Morocco. Senegal won the match in January but was stripped of the title in March, when it was awarded to Morocco.

items.title: DR Congo and Kenya agree to restore ties
items.summary: After years of strained relations over the conflict in eastern Congo, Kinshasa and Nairobi are moving towards a diplomatic reset. DR Congo's President Felix Tshisekedi met his Kenyan counterpart William Ruto over the weekend and they agreed to to restore normal ties and deepen economic and regional cooperation. Emmet Livingstone reports.

items.title: AFCON: Ten months on, court to rule on 2025 winner
items.summary: Ten months after the Africa Cup of Nations final was chaotically played on the field between Morocco and Senegal, the title will be awarded Tuesday by sports’ highest court. The Court of Arbitration for Sport set the target Monday to publish the verdict of its panel of three judges on Senegal’s appeal to regain the title the team won on the field in Morocco in January and then lost in a legal case in March.
